paper_metadata.title: An assessment of Ir–Pt–Al alloys for high-temperature materials

evidence.quote: Eight-gram button ingots of eight Ir–Pt–Al alloys were prepared by arc melting in an argon atmosphere.

The fracture strain of the Ir–5Pt–16Al alloy was 20% and it was better than that at 8% in the Ir–Nb alloys [1].
In the ternary alloys, the lowest minimum creep rate is observed in the Ir–5Pt–16Al (fcc1IrAl) and the Ir–25Pt–5Al (fcc 1Pt Al) alloys (about 3–4 3 10^−5 s^−1)
This suggests that the composition around 10 at% Pt is most effective in solid-solution hardening at 1773 K under 30 MPa.
